title: Random-Duration Switchback Designs under a Stationary Horvitz-Thompson Risk Criterion
banked_reason: The maximized paper is sound, but D0.5.G grades it incremental with paper-score ceiling 6.1 below the field floor 7.4; no bounded same-topic repair is tier-moving.
gap_reasons: It does not show that the construction beats the optimized two-rate family or is optimal in any meaningful design class, so the delivered contribution is a local benchmark correction rather than a sharp design frontier.

Its operational force is further limited because the mechanism relies on arbitrarily short dwell times, with the short component supported below 1/4096 of the carryover horizon, and establishes neither switching-cost or latency robustness nor finite-horizon improvement.
The narrow comparator scope and unresolved practical relevance keep the result below field tier and constrain its leading-journal score.
proof_attempt_summary: The run strengthened the marked-reset family from rate 3 to the near-elbow rate 7/2, proved exact boundary risk 72/7, packaged a fail-closed 2,390-leaf certificate for legal risk at most 10.3, and certified separation from Hu's rounded-design neighborhood. Both final mathematical panels passed, but the contribution remained a local benchmark improvement rather than a sharp design frontier; reaching field tier would require a new global theorem over the optimized two-rate family or a separate operational-robustness project.
tldr: Can a legal random-duration switchback improve Hu's published rounded two-rate design under exactly Hu's stationary pure-exposure HT criterion and Appendix horizon-specific second-moment outcome class? The formally amended same-family choice is \(G_q=(1-q)\operatorname{Unif}(0,q^2)+q\mathcal{L}(1+\operatorname{Exp}(7/2))\). The convenient rational rate \(7/2\) lies near the imbalance--contamination elbow: its marked boundary has exact risk \(72/7\), and the released immutable rate-\(7/2\) artifact with its fail-closed verifier certifies \(R(G_q)\le103/10\) for every \(0<q\le1/64\). The same verified artifact separates this legal family from Hu's rounded law and its certified radius-\(0.0005\) parameter box. The analysis retains reset marks, derives exact covariance and spectral laws, and supplies an equilibrium sampler, but makes no global-optimum, unrestricted-family, or pointwise-bounded-class dominance claim.
gap: Hu derives the exact spectral risk criterion and reports a strong two-rate design from numerical optimization, but does not study vanishing-duration mixtures, retained reset marks, uniform boundary recovery, certified all-frequency bounds, or a rigorous neighborhood comparison around its published parameters.
fill: The project will prove the boundary mechanism and exact \(32/3\) risk analytically, recover it uniformly with the explicit legal family, validate the continuum-wide \(43/4\) certificate and local benchmark lower certificate, and supply a normalized equilibrium sampler.
